text.p: Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banorte said on Thursday its net profits were 282.3 million pesos in the first half of the year, up 53 percent from 184.6 million pesos in the first half of 1996.

Othon Ruiz Montemayor, director general of the financial group, said the acquisition of Bancentro that was finalized on June 30 placed Banorte eighth in Mexico in terms of assets among financial groups.
The group's bank unit made a net profit of 134.3 million pesos in the first six months of the year, down from 140.6 million pesos in the first half of 1996, Ruiz said.
"Our profit level is satisfactory," Ruiz told a press conference. "We continue being a very productive and profitable bank, but all of the bank's problems have not been overcome."
The bank's capitalization level at the end of the second quarter was 15 percent, well above the nine percent required by the National Bank and Securities Commission, he said.
Past-due loans for the bank totalled 2.365 billion pesos at the end of the second quarter, down 212 million from the end of the first quarter this year, he said.
